Short Answer (3M).q: List any three physical properties of metals.
Short Answer (3M).a:
1. Lustrous (shiny appearance)
2. Malleable (can be hammered into sheets)
3. Ductile (can be drawn into wires)

Short Answer (3M).q: Why are non-metals generally poor conductors of electricity?
Short Answer (3M).a:
1. Non-metals have no free electrons.
2. They do not have mobile charge carriers.
3. Their electrons are tightly bound in covalent bonds.

Short Answer (3M).q: Give one example each of a metal reacting with water and with acid.
Short Answer (3M).a:
1. Metal with water: Sodium reacts with water to form sodium hydroxide and hydrogen.
2. Metal with acid: Zinc reacts with hydrochloric acid to form zinc chloride and hydrogen.

Short Answer (3M).q: Explain why iron nails get corroded when kept in copper sulphate solution.
Short Answer (3M).a:
1. Iron is more reactive than copper.
2. Iron displaces copper from copper sulphate solution.
3. The reaction forms iron sulphate and copper deposits on iron, causing corrosion.

Short Answer (3M).q: Name two metals which are extracted by electrolysis and give reason.
Short Answer (3M).a:
1. Sodium: It is highly reactive and cannot be extracted by reduction with carbon.
2. Aluminium: It is also highly reactive and requires electrolysis to break down its oxide.

Short Answer (3M).q: What is corrosion? Give one method of prevention.
Short Answer (3M).a:
1. Corrosion is the gradual destruction of metals by chemical reactions with the environment.
2. One method: Painting the metal surface to prevent contact with moisture and oxygen.

Short Answer (3M).q: Suggest two uses of graphite based on its properties.
Short Answer (3M).a:
1. As pencil lead because it is soft and leaves a mark on paper.
2. As electrodes in batteries because it conducts electricity.

Medium Answer(4m).q: Explain the reactivity series of metals and its importance in predicting chemical reactions.
Medium Answer(4m).a: The reactivity series arranges metals in order of decreasing reactivity: Potassium > Sodium > Calcium > Magnesium > Aluminium > Zinc > Iron > Tin > Lead > Hydrogen > Copper > Mercury > Silver > Gold. It helps predict displacement reactions, extraction methods, and corrosion prevention.
Medium Answer(4m).explanation: Metals higher in the series displace lower ones from compounds. For competitive exams, remember the mnemonic 'Please Stop Calling Me A Cute Zebra, I Like Her Call Smart Goat' for K Na Ca Mg Al Zn Fe Sn Pb H Cu Hg Ag Au. This series is based on tendency to lose electrons, crucial for redox reactions.

Medium Answer(4m).q: Describe the process of galvanization and explain why it prevents rusting.
Medium Answer(4m).a: Galvanization involves coating iron with a layer of zinc. Zinc acts as a sacrificial anode, corroding first and protecting the iron underneath.
Medium Answer(4m).explanation: Zinc is more reactive than iron, so it oxidizes preferentially. This forms a barrier and prevents water/oxygen contact. In exams, link to electrochemical series; zinc's higher reactivity makes it ideal for cathodic protection.

Medium Answer(4m).q: Compare the physical properties of metals and non-metals with suitable examples.
Medium Answer(4m).a: Metals are lustrous, malleable, ductile, good conductors; e.g., copper wire. Non-metals are dull, brittle, poor conductors; e.g., sulphur powder. Exceptions: mercury (liquid metal), graphite (conducting non-metal).
Medium Answer(4m).explanation: Properties stem from atomic structure: metals have free electrons for conductivity, non-metals have bound electrons. For HOTS, discuss why graphite conducts despite being non-metal—due to delocalized electrons in layers, aiding in layered conductivity.
